rows.question: When does my maternity leave start if my due date is 15 November 2026?
rows.reply:
Under the Mutterschutz (statutory maternity protection period) rules, your employer may not employ you during the last six weeks before the birth. This is the protection period before the birth. It is counted back from the expected day of delivery as stated in a certificate from a doctor or midwife. With an expected date of 15 November 2026, those six weeks fall in early October 2026. The exact first day follows from the date on your certificate.

You can still work during these six weeks if you expressly declare that you are willing to. You can withdraw that declaration at any time, with effect for the future.

If the baby does not arrive on the expected day, the period before the birth becomes shorter or longer to match. After the birth, your employer may not employ you for eight weeks. This rises to twelve weeks for premature births, multiple births, or if a disability is medically confirmed in the child within eight weeks. If the baby comes early, the period after the birth is also extended by the days lost before the birth.

You should tell your employer about the pregnancy and the expected delivery date as soon as you know. If your employer asks, you should provide a doctor's or midwife's certificate stating the expected date.

The maternity benefit paid by statutory health insurance covers this protection period. For payment before the birth, the doctor's or midwife's certificate of the expected date is what counts.

The Maternity Protection Act does not cover self-employed women. If you are self-employed, you need to arrange your own cover for the time before and after the birth.

rows.question: How long after birth can we apply for Elterngeld without losing money?
rows.reply:
The law does not set an application deadline. It limits how far back payment goes. Elterngeld (parental allowance) must be applied for in writing. It is paid retroactively only for the last three months of the child's life before the start of the life month in which the application is received. Earlier months are not paid.

Elterngeld can be drawn from the day of birth. Applications received later than three life months after the birth therefore lose whole months of payment from the start of the child's life.

The same three-month limit applies to changing an application. A change can reach back only to the last three life months before the life month in which the change request is received.

The Elterngeld office responsible for you receives the application and decides which months are paid.

rows.question: How much notice do I have to give my employer for Elternzeit?
rows.reply:
Elternzeit (parental leave (unpaid job-protected leave)) is not applied for. You request it from your employer. The law sets how far in advance:

- For Elternzeit before the child's third birthday: at the latest seven weeks before it starts.
- For Elternzeit between the third birthday and the eighth birthday: at the latest 13 weeks before it starts.

The request must be made to your employer in text form. The official family portal explains that this can be, for example, a letter without a signature or an email.

If you request Elternzeit for the period before the third birthday, you must at the same time state which periods within two years you will take.

The law allows a shorter period, as an exception, where there are urgent reasons. The family portal gives premature births as an example and says the period that applies then depends on the circumstances of the individual case. In that situation, notify your employer as early as possible.

If a mother cannot request Elternzeit in time for leave directly after her maternity protection period, for a reason she is not responsible for, she can make the request within one week after that reason ends.

For mothers who take Elternzeit straight after the maternity protection period, that period counts towards the two-year period mentioned above.

Your employer must confirm your Elternzeit to you. Protection against dismissal starts from the point you request Elternzeit, but at the earliest eight weeks before Elternzeit starts (before the third birthday), or 14 weeks before (between the third and eighth birthday).

rows.question: How long is maternity protection after the birth if the baby comes early?
rows.reply:
Mutterschutz (statutory maternity protection period) after the birth normally lasts eight weeks. During this time the employer may not employ the mother (MuSchG §3(2)).

If the baby comes early, two rules can apply.

First, if the baby is born before the expected date, the time before the birth is shorter than six weeks. The days lost before the birth are added to the period after the birth (MuSchG §3(1) and §3(2)). So the period after the birth is eight weeks plus those days.

Second, if the birth is a premature birth, the period after the birth is extended to twelve weeks (MuSchG §3(2) no. 1). The days lost before the birth are added on top of the twelve weeks as well (MuSchG §3(2)). The official family portal gives an example of a premature birth in the medical sense: a baby weighing less than 2,500 grams at birth. For a birth that is not medically premature, the portal says the total period stays at 14 weeks overall.

The statute also extends the period to twelve weeks for multiple births. It does the same if a disability in the child is medically established within eight weeks of the birth, but only if the mother applies for it (MuSchG §3(2)).

After the birth, the mother cannot choose to work during this period. There is an exception for school and university students who expressly ask to continue their studies (MuSchG §3(3)).

rows.question: Can my employer dismiss me while I am pregnant?
rows.reply:
In general, no. Under the Maternity Protection Act, an employer may not dismiss a woman during her pregnancy. The same Kündigungsschutz (protection against dismissal) lasts until the end of the protection period after the birth, and for at least four months after the birth. It also lasts for four months after a miscarriage after the twelfth week of pregnancy.

The protection depends on your employer knowing. It applies if your employer knew about the pregnancy when giving notice, or if you tell them within two weeks of receiving the notice. Missing those two weeks does no harm if the delay was not your fault and you tell them without delay. It applies even if you did not yet know you were pregnant, but you must already have been pregnant when the notice was given.

There is a narrow exception. The highest state authority responsible for occupational safety, or a body it designates, may declare a dismissal permissible in special cases that have nothing to do with the pregnancy, a miscarriage or the birth. Such a dismissal must be in writing and must state the reason. The official guidance gives examples such as insolvency, partial closure of the business, or a very serious breach of duty. Without the authority's approval, the dismissal is invalid.

If you are dismissed without that approval, the official guidance says you must bring a claim before the labour court. It says this is normally done within three weeks of receiving the written notice, and that if you do not bring a claim, the dismissal is treated as effective. You can file the claim yourself, through a lawyer, or orally at the court office. The guidance also recommends contacting the supervisory authority.

If you take parental leave after the birth, a separate Kündigungsschutz applies during that leave, again with exceptions only by approval of the same state authority.

Whether a particular dismissal is valid is decided by the labour court, and approval of an exception is decided by the state occupational-safety authority.

rows.question: Is there an income limit above which we get no Elterngeld?
rows.reply:
Yes. Under the statute, there is no entitlement to Elterngeld (parental allowance) if the entitled person had zu versteuerndes Einkommen (taxable income) of more than 175,000 euros in the last completed tax assessment period before the child's birth. If another person also meets the conditions, usually the other parent, the claim lapses when the two people's taxable income together is more than 175,000 euros.

The limit is on taxable income, not gross income. Taxable income is calculated by deducting items such as special expenses, provident expenses, individual allowances and extraordinary burdens from total income, so gross income is usually considerably higher. The Finanzamt determines taxable income, and it appears in the tax assessment notice. Attach the tax assessment notice for the calendar year before the birth to the application if you have it.

If that tax assessment notice is not yet available when you apply, you can still apply. Payment is then made provisionally, subject to revocation if the limit turns out to have been exceeded.

The official family portal says that different, higher limits applied to births before certain dates. The statutory excerpts I have do not include the transitional provision for earlier births, so I cannot say which limit applies to a particular birth. Whether the limit is exceeded in your case is decided by the Elterngeld office responsible for your application.

rows.question: How many months of Elterngeld can we get in total?
rows.reply:
The law sets the total in monthly amounts, counted by the child's months of life, not calendar months.

Basic form of Elterngeld (parental allowance): parents together are entitled to 12 monthly amounts. They are entitled to 2 further months (partner months) if one parent's earned income is reduced in two months of the child's life. One parent can receive at most 12 monthly amounts of the basic form.

Plus form: instead of one month of the basic form, a parent can take two months of the Plus form.

Partnership bonus: on top of this, each parent can receive at most 4 further monthly amounts as a partnership bonus. The official family portal says this is available when both parents work part-time at the same time.

Minimum and time limits: a parent is only entitled to Elterngeld if they receive it for at least two months of life. The basic form can be received until the end of the child's 14th month of life. The Plus form can be received until the end of the 32nd month of life, as long as from the 15th month at least one parent takes it in consecutive months. The portal adds that if there is a month after the 14th in which neither parent receives the Plus form, none can be received afterwards, even if months remain.

Months that count as used: months in which the mother receives maternity benefits that are offset under the law count as months of the basic form.

Premature births: the joint entitlement to the basic form rises to 13, 14, 15 or 16 monthly amounts if the child was born at least 6, 8, 12 or 16 weeks before the expected date of delivery shown on the doctor's or midwife's certificate. The per-parent maximum and the time limits rise accordingly.

How many months your family receives depends on how you split and combine these options. Only the responsible Elterngeld office decides your individual case.

rows.question: What is the Partnerschaftsbonus and who qualifies?
rows.reply:
The Partnerschaftsbonus (partnership bonus months) gives extra months of the parental allowance in its 'Plus' form to parents who both work part time at the same time.

What the law says (BEEG §4b):
- If both parents work no less than 24 and no more than 32 hours a week, averaged over a month of the child's life, and both meet the general conditions for parental allowance in §1, each parent gets an additional monthly amount for that month.
- Each parent can receive at most four bonus months.
- The bonus must be taken for at least two months.
- Both parents must take it at the same time, in consecutive months of the child's life.
- If, during or after the bonus period, it turns out the conditions were not met in every month applied for, the consecutive-months requirement still counts as met.
- If one parent comes to qualify as a sole recipient during the bonus period, that parent can continue receiving it alone.

One parent on their own (BEEG §4c): a parent can receive two to four additional months alone, if they work 24 to 32 hours a week on average in consecutive months, and one of these applies:
- they meet the tax conditions for the single-parent relief and the other parent lives with neither them nor the child;
- care by the other parent would endanger the child's welfare;
- care by the other parent is impossible, for example because of serious illness or severe disability. Economic reasons and being busy with other activities do not count.

How the amount works: the official family portal says the bonus is calculated the same way as the 'Plus' form of parental allowance, and is between 150 and 900 euros a month per parent, depending on income before the birth. The portal also says that if hours in a month fall below 24 or above 32, the bonus for that month must be paid back, for both parents. rows.question: We forgot to apply for Kindergeld. How far back will they pay?
rows.reply:
Kindergeld (child benefit) is paid retroactively only for the last six months before the start of the month in which your application is received. Months before that are not paid out. The law says this limit applies only to payment. The entitlement to Kindergeld itself is not affected by it.

Each month you wait before applying moves the six-month window forward, so earlier months drop out of payment.

Apply to the family benefits office at your local employment agency (Agentur für Arbeit). That office decides whether Kindergeld was due to you and for which months. For questions about applying, the Federal Employment Agency has a free service number: 0800 4 555530.

rows.question: How do we insure the baby after the birth?
rows.reply:
Under federal law, children of members of statutory health insurance are insured through Familienversicherung (free family cover for dependants). Children are covered up to their 18th birthday, and longer in certain cases, such as education or disability.

There is one important exception. Children are not covered if all of the following apply:
- the other parent, who is related to the child, is not a member of a statutory health insurance fund;
- that parent's total income is regularly above one twelfth of the annual earnings ceiling per month;
- that income is regularly higher than the insured parent's income.

In practice, the federal family portal says you must register the birth with the registry office for the place of birth within one week. The registry office issues the birth certificate, and you need that certificate to register the child with the health insurance fund.

rows.question: When are the first check-ups for the baby?
rows.reply:
The first check-ups for children in Germany follow the Kinder-Richtlinie (children's early-detection guideline). It sets ten check-ups in the first six years of life. These are the routine preventive check-ups, often called Vorsorgeuntersuchung (routine preventive check-up), and are named U1, U2 and so on.

The first four:
- U1: immediately after birth. It should be done within the first 30 minutes after the child is born. If no doctor is present but a midwife is, the midwife should do it.
- U2: 3rd to 10th day of life. Tolerance window: 3rd to 14th day.
- U3: 4th to 5th week of life. Tolerance window: 3rd to 8th week.
- U4: 3rd to 4th month of life. Tolerance window: 2nd to 4.5th month.

These periods also apply to babies born prematurely. The premature birth is taken into account when the results are assessed.

The G-BA's page notes that the published version does not yet include a decision that came into force on 20 August 2026. Your paediatrician can confirm the current periods.

rows.question: What is Mutterschaftsgeld and when do I apply for it?
rows.reply:
Mutterschaftsgeld (maternity pay from the health insurer) is a payment for the protection periods before and after the birth, and for the day of the birth itself.

Who pays depends on how the mother is insured:

- If she is a member of a statutory health insurance fund, the health insurance fund pays Mutterschaftsgeld under the statutory health insurance rules. For women in employment, it is based on average net daily pay over the last three calendar months before the protection period starts, up to a maximum of 13 euros per calendar day. The employer pays a supplement covering the difference between 13 euros and that average net daily pay.
- If she is not a member of a statutory health insurance fund, Mutterschaftsgeld is paid by the federal government, up to a total of 210 euros. It is paid on application by the Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung.

The protection periods normally begin 6 weeks before the expected due date and end 8 weeks after the birth. For payment before the birth, the law relies on a certificate from a doctor or midwife that gives the expected date of delivery. The right to Mutterschaftsgeld is suspended for as long as the mother receives pay that is subject to contributions, except for one-off payments.

When to apply: the sources available to me do not state an application deadline or say when the application should be made. They only say that payment before the birth is based on the doctor's or midwife's certificate. Ask your statutory health insurance fund how and when to apply. If you are not in statutory health insurance, ask the Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung.

Whether you qualify and how much you would receive is decided by your health insurance fund, or by the Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung if you are not statutorily insured.

rows.question: We are not married. Is my partner automatically the legal father?
rows.reply:
No. Under German law, a man is the legal father of a child if one of three things applies: he is married to the mother at the time of the birth, he has acknowledged paternity, or a court has established his paternity. A man who is not married to the mother at the birth does not become the legal father automatically.

The usual route is Vaterschaftsanerkennung (acknowledgement of paternity). It is voluntary and needs the mother's consent. The father and the mother must each make their declaration in person before a competent office, for example the youth welfare office, a registry office, a local court or a notary. The office records both declarations. Depending on the federal state, it may cost a fee at a notary or local court. The acknowledgement can be made before the child is born. It cannot be made subject to a condition or a time limit. It is not effective while another man's paternity exists, for example if the mother is married to someone else at the birth.

If the father does not want to acknowledge paternity, or the mother does not consent, the child, the mother or the presumed biological father can ask a court to establish paternity.

Acknowledging paternity does not by itself give the father parental custody. For unmarried parents, joint custody also needs declarations by both parents that they want joint custody, or a court decision, or the parents marrying after the birth. The youth welfare office advises on custody questions.

rows.question: How do unmarried parents get joint custody?
rows.reply:
If the parents are not married to each other when the child is born, the mother has parental custody alone at first. The law gives three ways for the parents to get joint custody.

1. Both parents declare that they want to take on custody together. This declaration is called a Sorgeerklärung (declaration of joint custody). Sorgeerklärungen can be made, for example, at the youth welfare office or before a notary. They can also be made before the birth.

2. The parents marry each other.

3. The family court transfers joint custody to both parents. One parent applies. The court transfers all or part of custody to both parents if this does not go against the child's welfare. If the other parent gives no reasons against it, and none are otherwise apparent, the law presumes that joint custody does not go against the child's welfare. In that case the court decides in a simplified procedure, without hearing the youth welfare office and without hearing the parents in person.

For the father, legal paternity comes first. He becomes the legal father by acknowledging the child with the mother's consent, or through a court finding of paternity. Acknowledging paternity does not by itself give him custody. A Sorgeerklärung or a court decision is still needed.

Your local youth welfare office gives advice on all questions about parental custody. The family court decides applications for joint custody.

rows.question: Will our baby automatically be German if we are both Indian citizens?
rows.reply:
Not automatically. The law sets conditions, and whether they are met for your child is decided by the authorities, not by this service.

German Staatsangehörigkeit (citizenship) by birth works in two ways under the Nationality Act.

By descent: a child acquires German Staatsangehörigkeit at birth if one parent holds German Staatsangehörigkeit. If neither parent is German, this route does not apply.

By birth in Germany: a child of foreign parents born in Germany acquires German Staatsangehörigkeit if one parent meets both of these conditions:
1. has had their lawful habitual residence in Germany for five years, and
2. holds an unlimited right of residence (or, for Swiss citizens and their family members, a residence permit under the EU–Switzerland free movement agreement).

If the child acquires German Staatsangehörigkeit this way, it is entered in the birth register in which the child's birth is recorded. Whether your family meets these conditions is assessed when the birth is registered. Only the responsible authority decides the individual case.

If the child does not acquire German Staatsangehörigkeit, the Residence Act has a separate rule. A child born in Germany is given a residence permit by the authorities on their own initiative if, at the time of birth, both parents (or the parent with sole custody) hold a residence permit, a settlement permit, or an EU long-term residence permit. If only one parent holds one of these, a residence permit can be granted. If a parent is in Germany on a visa or visa-free at the time of birth, the child's stay counts as permitted until that visa or visa-free stay ends.

The excerpts available here do not cover Indian citizenship rules for your child. For that, ask the Indian embassy or consulate responsible for where you live.

rows.question: We are getting Mutterschaftsgeld. Does that reduce our Elterngeld?
rows.reply:
Yes, as a general rule. The law says that Mutterschaftsgeld (maternity pay from the health insurer) is offset against Elterngeld (parental allowance). The same applies to the employer's top-up to Mutterschaftsgeld. BEEG §3(1) No. 1 lists both: Mutterschaftsgeld under the social insurance rules, and the employer top-up under MuSchG §20. The statute refers to these payments where they are due for the time from the day of the birth.

There is one exception. The one-off Mutterschaftsgeld of at most 210 euros is not offset. This is paid by the Federal Office for Social Security to women who are not members of a statutory health insurer, under MuSchG §19(2). BEEG §3(1) No. 1(a) excludes it from the offset.

If the maternity payments are due for only part of a month of the child's life, they are offset only against the matching part of Elterngeld (BEEG §3(1)). The official family portal explains the effect for the same child. If the maternity payments are higher than Elterngeld, only the maternity payments are paid. If Elterngeld is higher, the difference is paid as Elterngeld. The portal also says that months in which the mother receives maternity payments for the same child count as months of basic Elterngeld for her. This applies even if the payments are due for only one day of that month. The offset applies only to the mother's Elterngeld, not to the father's.

This explains the rule only. Whether and how much your Elterngeld is reduced is decided by the Elterngeld office that processes your application, not by this service.

rows.question: Can I work while receiving Elterngeld?
rows.reply:
Yes, the law allows some work. Under the federal Elterngeld law, one of the conditions for Elterngeld (parental allowance) is that the parent does no work or does not work full-time. The other conditions are living in Germany, living in the same household as the child, and caring for and raising the child yourself.

How much work counts as full-time is not set out in the statute sections provided here. The official family portal explains that you may work part-time while receiving Elterngeld, as long as you work no more than 32 hours a week. The portal says this explanation applies to children born after August 2021. Partly different rules apply to children born earlier, and the portal refers those parents to their Elterngeld office.

Working affects the amount. The law sets a maximum of 1,800 euros a month for full months in which you have no earned income. For months after the birth in which you earn less than before the birth, Elterngeld is paid as a percentage of the difference between the two incomes. For this calculation, income before the birth counts up to at most 2,770 euros. The portal notes that if you work part-time, a variant paid over twice as many months may be worth considering.

If your application says you expect to earn income during the payment period, the amount is first decided provisionally. After the payment period ends, you must prove your actual earned income for that time. The portal says employees need a certificate from their employer about their working hours during the payment period. Self-employed parents give their own statement about their working hours.

Whether you qualify, and how much you would receive while working, is decided by the Elterngeld office responsible for you.

Where: you apply to the Familienkasse responsible for the district where you live. If you have no residence in Germany, it is the Familienkasse where you usually stay. How: the law says Kindergeld (child benefit) must be applied for in writing. The official family portal says you can apply electronically or in writing, using the Familienkassen form. You can fill it in online, then print and sign it. For a newborn child, you can apply fully online with a valid ELSTER certificate, with no printing or handwritten signature.

What to include: the application must give your tax identification number and your child's tax identification number. For a child under 18, these are usually the only proof needed. If your child was born abroad or lives abroad, include a copy of the foreign birth certificate or another official document that confirms the birth.

Who applies: Kindergeld is paid to only one person per child. If the child lives in the parents' shared household, the parents decide between themselves who receives it. If they do not decide, the family court decides on request.

After you apply: if the Familienkasse needs more documents, it tells you the date by which to send them. If you miss that date, your application can be delayed or refused. Documents can be sent through the online service.

Applying late: the family portal says Kindergeld can be paid retroactively for up to 6 months, if you were entitled but it was not paid. In the application, state that you are applying retroactively and from when.

For questions about applying, the Bundesagentur für Arbeit has a free service line: 0800 4 555530. The Familienkasse decides your individual claim.

rows.question: What are the Elterngeld rules for a self-employed parent in Bavaria?
rows.reply:
Bavarian state procedures are not covered here. We cover federal law, Hessen procedures and the Indian consular track. For Bavaria-specific forms and offices, contact the Elterngeld (parental allowance) office responsible for where you live in Bavaria. The federal rules below apply everywhere in Germany, including Bavaria.

Who can claim. A person can claim Elterngeld if they live or usually stay in Germany, live in one household with the child, care for and raise the child themselves, and work not at all or not full-time.

Self-employed income counts. Elterngeld is based on income from work before the birth. This includes positive income from a trade or business (Gewerbebetrieb) and from self-employed work, as well as from employment and agriculture or forestry, minus taxes and social contributions. It must be income taxable in Germany.

How much the law sets. Elterngeld is 67 percent of that pre-birth income. For full months with no income from work, it is paid up to a maximum of 1,800 euros a month. For incomes below 1,000 euros the percentage rises, up to 100 percent. For incomes above 1,200 euros it falls, down to 65 percent. It is paid at a minimum of 300 euros, even with no income before the birth. If you earn less after the birth than before, Elterngeld is paid on the difference, and pre-birth income counts up to 2,770 euros at most.

When your tax assessment is not yet available. Elterngeld is decided provisionally, based on the information you make credible, in three cases. The first is when the tax assessment notice for the last completed tax year before the birth is not yet available and it cannot yet be said whether the income limits in the law are exceeded. The second is when pre-birth income cannot be determined. The third is when you expect to have income from work during the payment period.

If your application estimated income from work, you must prove your actual income for that period after the payment period ends. If you stated that you expect no income from work during the payment period, Elterngeld is paid subject to revocation if you do have such income. It is also paid subject to revocation if your tax assessment is missing and you stated that the income limits will not be exceeded, but they are.

How long. Parents together can claim 12 monthly payments of basic Elterngeld. They get 2 more if one parent's income from work is reduced for two months. One parent can claim at most 12, plus up to 4 partnership bonus months. Each parent must claim for at least two months. One month of basic Elterngeld can be taken as two months of Elterngeld Plus.

The excerpts do not include the detailed rule on how self-employed profit is worked out, or which period is used to measure it. Whether you qualify and how much you would receive is decided only by the Elterngeld office responsible for you in Bavaria.

rows.question: Can you fill in our Elterngeld application form for us?
rows.reply:
We cannot fill in your Elterngeld (parental allowance) application for you. The entries on the form are decisions about your own family, such as which months you claim and what income you declare. Making those choices for you would be an individual case assessment, which we are not allowed to do. Only the Elterngeld office responsible for you decides your application.

What the law says about the application itself:

- Elterngeld must be applied for in writing.
- The application must state which months of the child's life you claim the basic amount for, which months the Plus version, and which months the partnership bonus.
- Payment is made retroactively only for the last three months of the child's life before the month in which the application is received. Earlier months are not paid.
- The application must be signed by the person applying. The other parent entitled to the allowance must also sign to confirm they have seen it. This does not apply where one person alone has parental custody, or in one special case the law sets out separately.
- The choices made in the application can be changed until the end of the payment period. A change can be backdated only for the last three months before the month the change request is received. Except in cases of special hardship, months already paid out cannot be changed.

Documents the official family portal lists for the application include:

- your child's birth certificate
- proof of your previous income. For employees, this means payslips for the last 12 months: for mothers, the 12 months before the month maternity protection begins; for fathers, the 12 months before the birth. For the self-employed, this is usually the latest tax assessment.

The portal notes that further documents may be needed depending on the case.

Who decides: the responsible authority is the one the state has designated for the district where the child lives at the time of the first application. The family portal calls this your Elterngeld office. That office is also the place to ask for help with the form.

rows.question: Based on our situation, will our Elterngeld application be approved?
rows.reply:
We cannot say whether your application will be approved. Only the authority that handles your application decides that, based on your documents. That is your local Elterngeld office (Elterngeldstelle).

What the law says in general:

Under the federal statute, a person is entitled to Elterngeld (parental allowance) if they:
1. have their residence or habitual stay in Germany,
2. live in one household with the child,
3. care for and raise the child themselves, and
4. work not at all or not full-time.

The statute also sets out exceptions. For example, some people posted abroad are covered, as are some people who live with a child they are adopting.

Elterngeld must be applied for in writing. It is paid backwards in time only for the last three months of the child's life before the month in which the Elterngeldstelle receives the application. Earlier months are not paid.

If you disagree with the Elterngeldstelle's decision, you can object to it. This is called a Widerspruch. It must be made in writing to the Elterngeldstelle within one month of receiving the decision letter. Court cases against the decision go to the social courts.

To find out whether you qualify, submit your application to the Elterngeldstelle responsible for where you live. In Hessen, that is the office for your area.

rows.question: How much tax will we save if I switch to Steuerklasse 3 before the birth?
rows.reply:
We cannot tell you how much tax you would save by switching tax class. That is a calculation for your household, and tax class choice and its tax effects belong to a Steuerberater or the Finanzamt. The excerpts we have also do not describe the tax effect of switching.

What the excerpts do cover is how your tax class is used when the parental allowance is calculated:

- The law says the income tax deduction in the parental allowance calculation is based on your tax class and, where relevant, the factor under § 39f of the Income Tax Act. Tax class VI is not taken into account.
- If you changed tax class before the birth, the most recent tax class is used for the simplified net income calculation. The older tax class is used only if it applied for longer than the newer one within the whole assessment period.
- If you work after the birth, the same deduction details are used as before the birth. Changing tax class again after the birth has no further effect on the parental allowance.
- The Elterngeldstelle calculates this net figure itself from your gross income, using a simplified method. The result can differ from the net pay on your payslip.

Whether a switch makes sense for your family, and what it would change, is not something we can assess. For the tax effect, ask a Steuerberater or the Finanzamt. For how your parental allowance is calculated, the Elterngeldstelle decides.
